subject: chemistry
title: Colour Cosmos: Test Tube Tales
welcome_lead: Identify transition metal ions by their characteristic colour changes.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on identification of transition metal aqua ions.
final_note: You've decoded the rainbow of test-tube chemistry.

concepts.def: Reacts with both acid and base.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Adding NaOH gives a coloured hydroxide precipitate. Cu^2+ -> blue Cu(OH)2. Fe^2+ -> green Fe(OH)2 (browns in air to Fe(OH)3).

Fe^3+ -> orange/brown Fe(OH)3. Al^3+ -> white Al(OH)3 (dissolves in excess NaOH as [Al(OH)4]-).

Few drops NH3 -> same hydroxide ppt as NaOH.

Excess NH3: Cu(OH)2 dissolves as deep blue [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]^2+. Most others stay precipitated.

[Cu(H2O)6]^2+ + 4Cl- -> [CuCl4]^2- (yellow). Reversible by dilution with water.

[Co(H2O)6]^2+ (pink) + 4Cl- -> [CoCl4]^2- (blue). Shift seen in 'cobalt chloride' moisture indicator.

mcqs.q: Why are most transition metal complex ions coloured?
options: Ligands split the d-orbitals into two energy levels; electrons absorb visible light to jump between them (d-d transitions), and the complementary colour is transmitted.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
Transition metals are coloured because their nuclei emit photons in the visible range.
Transition metal ions are coloured because they have a half-full d-subshell which naturally absorbs light.

mcqs.q: Why can transition metals show variable oxidation states?
options: Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they can gain protons easily.
Transition metals are coloured because their nuclei emit photons in the visible range.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they have many shells of electrons.
The 4s and 3d orbitals are similar in energy, so different numbers of electrons can be removed without a large energy cost.

mcqs.q: What kind of bond forms between a ligand and a central metal ion in a complex?
options: The ligand forms an ionic bond with the metal because the metal is positively charged.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they can gain protons easily.
A dative (coordinate) covalent bond — the ligand donates a lone pair into an empty orbital on the metal.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Fe^2+ aq”?
options: Reacts with both acid and base.
